correctness.rationale: Adjacency preserves the unique order-\(p\) subgroup of each cyclic vertex subgroup, while a common order-\(p\) subgroup gives a length-at-most-two path, so components are exactly indexed by order-\(p\) subgroups. A nonidentity prime-order element is universal in its component. This yields the sharp two-per-component lower and upper bounds, with the involution-square criterion exactly characterizing nontrivial components when \(p=2\).

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies two standard strengthened domination parameters for proper power graphs of finite prime-power groups. It identifies the exact \(2\)-group obstruction, proves that every minimum total dominating set is paired, and gives the concrete abelian criterion excluding direct \(C_2\)-factors.
